Call D1 · both portals

Which headings wear the condensed face?

Stage 4 was asked whether the page title keeps the condensed face. The census widened it. Today the condensed face is on page titles, most card and section titles, and nearly every window title, in the admin and the coaches portal alike. One shared rule puts it there. The written target says otherwise: your F2 ruling and the sweep plan put titles in the plain face, and A3 moved card and section titles there. Stage 3 acted on A3, and those few titles are the plain ones you see today.

So the call is whether to finish the written target or change it. Capitals are not part of it: column and band headings keep the condensed face in every option. Each picture is the live dev screen in Warm at true size. The option pictures are the same page with the face changed in the browser; nothing was saved.

Option 1 (recommended)Every heading in the plain face, the page title included.
Option 2Every heading in the condensed face, including the titles Stage 3 moved.
Option 3The page title alone stays condensed, one size up (24 px). Every other heading is plain.
Option 4Leave it mixed, as the today pictures show.

What decides it: the step from page title to card title

Condensed letters read about a size smaller than plain ones. So a condensed page title over plain card titles loses its place at the top. Below, the top of Organization → Settings: the page title “Settings” over the first card’s title, “Your public site”.

Today

The coaches portal → Money (1440) RESTYLED

The coaches portal shares this call (A6, one part, one look). Its page title “Money” and the headline “Start with your season budget” are condensed today. The tile titles and the team name (“15U AAA”) are already plain, from your 2 August pick, and the team name stays plain in every option. The “Build your budget” button is condensed too; a button is the plain face, so it changes in every option. These pictures leave it as it is.

Why option 1. Only options 1 and 2 keep a clear step from page title to card title. Of those two, option 1 is the written target (F2, A3 and the plan’s role table). It keeps Stage 3’s walked titles. It also avoids the closed-up lowercase that option 2 shows at 16 px, which is the reason behind your 2 August pick. The case against it: the condensed face is the product’s display voice, and option 1 takes it off every screen’s title in both portals. It would stay only in capitals and on the public pages. You have walked condensed page titles for months. Option 2 changes about ten places and keeps the product as you have seen it; its cost is the 16 px headings. I first recommended option 3 (condensed page title only). The step pictures above changed my mind: even at 24 px, the page title barely clears the card title under it.

What the design review changed

The design review read these drawings against the product’s written rules before you saw them. Applied: D1’s recommendation moved from “condensed page title only” to “every heading plain”, after it found the condensed page title reading no larger than the card titles under it. I re-took that picture one size larger to check, and added it as option 3. D1 now opens from the written target (F2, A3) instead of saying nothing was written. A team’s name stays plain in every option. The savings line is plain text, not a chip. The Match typed locations foot line is set at the 12 px reading size, not the 10 px chip size. The Tiers sentence is a 12 px caption under its eyebrow. Two spacing changes too small to see are marked as such. D2 now says that it replaces the coaches drawer’s dark fill and that two chosen “All”s share a tint. Declined: nothing. One finding reversed a row: the sample email’s head in Send email stays as it is, because it draws the real email, and the real email’s head is set that way.

What Stage 3 handed over

Stage 3’s guard left about 40 lines unmarked in the files it touched. Read one by one, most are labels already in an allowed role (a chip, a column heading, a step number, a web address, a count beside a heading). The build marks each one with its role so the guard stops counting it, and nothing changes on screen. The rest are real faults and are on tab 2: first-run setup’s titles at 900 in the typewriter face, five billing titles at 800, three billing eyebrows, the count beside a section title in capitals, a draft schedule’s score at 800, and Bring in a team’s labels. Three dead styles go to Stage 5 (dead code).

Not in this stage: the rest of the guard’s report (about 100 lines in the tournament schedule styles, house league’s legacy branches, the old tournament toolbar). Most of it is dead code that Stage 5 deletes. The guard only counts it, and it is not on any screen.

Your calls · Stage 4

Three calls

D1 is the heading question, widened from the page title to every heading. D2 is the toggle Stage 3 left. D3 came out of re-checking the list. Everything on tab 2 that no call touches follows a recipe you have already ruled on, so it needs no call. Each call carries my recommendation. Pick, add a note if you like, then build the paste-back at the bottom. Nothing gets built until you rule.

D1 · Which headings wear the condensed face?

The written target already answers part of this. Your F2 ruling and the sweep plan put titles in the plain face, and A3 moved card and section titles there. The code never followed it for most titles. One shared rule makes every heading condensed unless the heading says otherwise, so page titles, most card titles and nearly every window title are condensed today, in both portals. Stage 3 moved its titles to the plain face “as the coaches portal’s sections do”. That reason was wrong (the portal’s sections are condensed too), but A3’s ruling stands on its own. So the call is whether to finish the written target or change it. The pictures settle one thing. Condensed letters read about a size smaller than plain ones, so a condensed page title over plain card titles loses its place at the top: at 20 px, and still at 24 px.

Rides on it. Option 1 changes the one shared heading rule plus about 30 titles that set the condensed face themselves: the page header in both portals, the shared window title, club card titles and house league window titles. The code change is small, but every screen looks different. Option 2 changes about ten places. In every option, a team’s name stays plain (your 2 August pick), and a button set in the condensed face (the coaches portal’s “Build your budget”) goes to the plain face, because it is a button.

D2 · The Unread / All toggle: one “chosen” look

One part has three looks. On the notifications page the chosen half is a khaki fill. In the bell’s drawer it is a solid olive fill in the admin and a solid dark ink fill in the coaches portal. The page’s note says it was built to match the drawer, so the drift was not intended. On the page, the toggle sits on the same row as the All / Needs attention / Activity pills, whose chosen pill is an olive tint with an olive edge.

Rides on it: two rules in two files. The drawer is shared, so it changes in both portals.

D3 · Account → Notification settings is not an admin screen

The list placed C65 (the BELL / PUSH / EMAIL column headings) in org settings. They are on Account → Notification settings, the page every signed-in person reaches from the account menu, admins included. The column headings are a small part of it. Whole sentences on that page are in the typewriter face (“Signed in as…”, “Mutes everything except the alerts below”, “Organization access”). No project owns the page: the public-face plan treats the account tab as already done.

Rides on it: one page, about ten rules. It also holds the “Turn on notifications on this device” tester.
